xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for AOT-2: Add user profile settings with validation

plan.title: Add user profile settings with validation
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5

narratives.Problem: The issue asks for a /settings/profile route, a reusable profile form over name/email/timezone, client-side validation, an API endpoint that saves through a repository or service layer rather than inline route logic, clear success and error states, a nav link, and tests for invalid email, missing required fields and a successful save. None of it exists at fdf7000: `find app -type f` returns four page files and five component files, with no app/settings/, no app/api/ and no app/lib/; app/components/Nav.tsx:7-12 lists exactly four links; `next build` prerenders only /, /_not-found, /about, /contact and /pricing. Three properties of the existing tree decide the sequencing because each one breaks a naive implementation silently. First, vitest.config.mts:9 sets include to __tests__/**/*.test.tsx, so a non-JSX test written as __tests__/foo.test.ts is never collected while npm test still exits 0 and prints a green summary. Second, __tests__/Nav.test.tsx:38-60 asserts the nav link list exactly, toEqual(['Home','About','Pricing','Contact']) plus getAllByRole('link') toHaveLength(5), and the comment at line 41 says that exactness is deliberate, so a fifth nav entry fails that file unless the same commit updates it. Third, @testing-library/user-event is not a dependency, so interaction tests must use fireEvent. One ambiguity was settled empirically during planning rather than left to the work agent: Web Request, Response, Response.json() and fetch are all available in this vitest jsdom environment, verified with a throwaway probe, so route-handler tests need no environment pragma.
narratives.Proposal: Ship the feature as a chain of small vertical slices, each independently reviewable and each leaving the tree green. The persistence path is a three-module stack under app/lib/profile/, this repo's first non-component module directory: validation.ts holds the pure rules, the ProfileInput/ProfileErrors types and a fixed six-entry TIMEZONES list; repository.ts holds one module-level record plus getProfile/saveProfile/resetProfile; service.ts composes both into saveUserProfile() returning a discriminated { ok: true, profile } | { ok: false, errors } result. app/api/profile/route.ts is a thin POST handler that coerces the JSON body to three strings, calls saveUserProfile, and maps ok:false to HTTP 400 with the error map and ok:true to HTTP 200 with the saved profile; it contains no regex, no validation branch and no storage variable, which is the small repository/service layer the issue asks for. app/components/ProfileForm.tsx is the reusable client component and imports the same validateProfile the server uses, so a rule can never be enforced in one place and not the other; it validates on submit, renders per-field error text, and only issues the fetch when the client-side check is clean. app/settings/profile/page.tsx is a thin Server Component that mounts it, matching how every other page in the repo is written. Sequencing follows the traps: the vitest glob widens first because five later items add .test.ts files, and the nav link ships together with its test update in one item.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No real database, file, cookie, or localStorage persistence; the mock repository is one in-process record that resets on server restart
- No authentication, authorization, session, or per-user profile record
- No GET /api/profile endpoint and no hydration of saved values into the form
- No new runtime or dev dependency in package.json
- No zod or other schema library, and no react-hook-form
- No @testing-library/user-event; interaction tests use fireEvent
- No RFC-5322-complete email validation and no MX or deliverability check
- No full IANA timezone list and no timezone auto-detection
- No server actions; the form posts to the route handler
- No avatar upload, password change, or notification preferences
- No changes to the content of /, /about, /pricing, or /contact
- No fix for the pre-existing ESLint warning from .claude/skills/stitch-react-components/examples/gold-standard-card.tsx; AOT-1 owns it
- No README rewrite; AOT-1 owns that, so this branch appends a section only
- No CI workflow
- No Playwright or browser-based verification

autoDecisions.summary: Add no new runtime or dev dependency: hand-write the validation instead of pulling in zod, and drive form tests with fireEvent instead of adding @testing-library/user-event.
autoDecisions.rationale: package.json carries three runtime dependencies and the issue asks to keep the implementation simple and consistent with the existing architecture. Validation over three fields is about twenty lines, and the existing suite already drives interactions without user-event (__tests__/Button.test.tsx:37).

autoDecisions.summary: Validate email with /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ rather than an RFC-5322 pattern.
autoDecisions.rationale: It rejects the cases a user actually hits — no @, no domain, no dot, embedded spaces — without pretending to implement the full grammar. Full correctness is listed as a NonGoal so a reviewer does not read the simple pattern as an oversight.

autoDecisions.summary: Make timezone a <select> over a fixed six-entry TIMEZONES array exported from validation.ts, with a leading empty option as the invalid state.
autoDecisions.rationale: It makes 'timezone is required' enforceable identically on client and server. Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') would return several hundred entries and make test output depend on the host ICU build.

autoDecisions.summary: Store one profile in a module-level variable with a resetProfile() test seam, rather than keying records by user.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says mock persistence is acceptable, and the app has no auth and no user identity, so there is nothing to key a record by. The reset export exists because module state survives between tests in a file.

autoDecisions.summary: Expose POST /api/profile only, with no GET and no hydration of saved values into the form.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for a simple endpoint for saving profile data. A load path is extra surface nothing in the issue requires, so it is recorded as a NonGoal instead of built.

autoDecisions.summary: Coerce a malformed or non-object JSON body to three empty strings and return the ordinary 400 validation-error map.
autoDecisions.rationale: It avoids inventing a second error shape for a case the browser form cannot produce, and keeps ProfileErrors keyed only by field name so the client renders it with one code path.

autoDecisions.summary: Run validation on submit, not on change or blur.
autoDecisions.rationale: All three required test cases are submit-driven, and on-change validation flags a field the user has not finished typing.

autoDecisions.summary: Widen vitest include to __tests__/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} rather than naming every non-JSX test file .tsx.
autoDecisions.rationale: One config line beats a naming convention every future contributor has to be told about, and the failure it prevents is silent: an uncollected test file still reports a green run.

autoDecisions.summary: Append a '## Profile settings' section to README.md instead of restructuring the file.
autoDecisions.rationale: AOT-1 is in flight on a sibling branch with a full README rewrite. Appending at the end keeps both branches mergeable.

autoDecisions.summary: Skip Playwright and browser-based verification entirely for this issue.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every acceptance criterion is checkable from the diff, npm test, npm run lint, or npm run build, so no item needs a running server or an isolated browser profile.

narrative.Action: Create app/lib/profile/validation.ts exporting: type ProfileInput = { name: string; email: string; timezone: string }; type ProfileErrors = Partial<Record<keyof ProfileInput, string>>; a six-entry `as const` array TIMEZONES = ["UTC", "America/New_York", "America/Los_Angeles", "Europe/London", "Europe/Budapest", "Asia/Tokyo"]; and validateProfile(input: ProfileInput): ProfileErrors. Rules: a name that trims to empty sets errors.name = "Name is required."; an email that trims to empty sets errors.email = "Email is required." and otherwise a trimmed email failing /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ sets errors.email = "Enter a valid email address."; an empty timezone sets errors.timezone = "Timezone is required." and a non-empty timezone outside TIMEZONES sets errors.timezone = "Choose a timezone from the list.". Keep the EMAIL_PATTERN const module-private. This module is imported by both the browser form and the server route, so the rules exist in exactly one place. Add __tests__/profileValidation.test.ts covering each branch.

narrative.Action: Create app/lib/profile/service.ts exporting type SaveProfileResult = { ok: true; profile: ProfileInput } | { ok: false; errors: ProfileErrors } and saveUserProfile(input: ProfileInput): SaveProfileResult. The body calls validateProfile(input); when the returned map has any key it returns { ok: false, errors } WITHOUT touching the repository; otherwise it returns { ok: true, profile: saveProfile(input) }. This is the one call the route handler makes. Add __tests__/profileService.test.ts calling resetProfile() in beforeEach.

metadata.sizeJustification: 17 files, under the 25-file limit. The 14-subsystem count is an artifact of the heuristic: it derives a subsystem from a path's first two segments, and this repo keeps every test in one flat __tests__/ directory, so each of the seven test files counts as its own subsystem. The real subsystems are four — app/lib/profile, app/api/profile, app/components, app/settings/profile — plus __tests__ and two root files (vitest.config.mts, README.md). The slices are also genuinely inseparable as sibling issues: the form, the route handler and the page all import the same validation module, and the nav link would point at a 404 until the page ships, so splitting them across issues would land broken intermediate states on main.
